response: SAI-RAG is an educational question-answering assistant that retrieves relevant information from a local FAQ knowledge base before generating an answer.
The project uses Python LangChain FAISS sentence-transformer embeddings Google Gemini and Streamlit.
RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It retrieves relevant documents and supplies them as context to a language model before generation.
FAISS is a library for efficient similarity search over dense vectors. In this project it is used as the local vector store.
Embeddings convert text into numerical vectors so the system can compare the meaning of a question with the meaning of knowledge-base entries.
It embeds the FAQ knowledge base retrieves the most relevant entries for a question and sends that context to Gemini with instructions to answer only from the supplied context.
Yes. SAI-RAG can answer course and learning questions when the requested information is present in its knowledge base.

prompt: Why does the first question take longer?
